text:
As the world works to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and combat climate change, sustainable fuels are becoming a vital part of the global energy transition. Produced from renewable resources or low-carbon processes, these fuels provide cleaner alternatives to conventional fossil fuels while helping industries reduce their environmental impact without compromising performance.

Sustainable fuels include a wide range of energy sources, such as Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), renewable diesel, biodiesel, biogas, biomethane, renewable hydrogen, and synthetic fuels (e-fuels). Each plays a unique role in cutting emissions across sectors including aviation, shipping, road transport, manufacturing, and power generation.

One of the greatest advantages of sustainable fuels is that many can be used with existing engines, vehicles, and fuel infrastructure. This allows businesses to lower carbon emissions without the need for extensive equipment replacement, making the transition to cleaner energy more practical and cost-effective.

Technological innovation is accelerating the development of sustainable fuels. Advances in feedstock processing, renewable electricity, green hydrogen production, carbon capture, and fuel conversion technologies are improving efficiency while expanding production capacity. At the same time, governments are introducing supportive policies, incentives, and emissions reduction targets to encourage investment and increase market adoption.

Despite challenges such as production costs, feedstock availability, and supply chain development, the outlook for sustainable fuels remains strong. Continued collaboration between fuel producers, technology providers, policymakers, investors, and end users is helping scale production and create more resilient energy systems.

As demand for cleaner energy continues to grow, sustainable fuels will play an increasingly important role in helping hard-to-decarbonize sectors achieve their climate goals while supporting economic growth and long-term energy security.

Takeaway Point

Sustainable fuels provide a practical pathway to reducing carbon emissions across transportation and industry. Through innovation, investment, and collaboration, they are helping build a cleaner, more resilient energy future while supporting the global journey toward net-zero emissions.

text:
Signs agreement to purchase approximately 6,000 metric tons of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from Moeve, covering around 50% of DHL Express’ annual fuel consumption at Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (MAD)

One-year agreement running from July 2026 to June 2027 supports DHL’s ambition to increase the use of sustainable aviation fuels

DHL Express, the world’s leading international express logistics provider, and Moeve announced the signing of a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) offtake agreement at Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (MAD). Under the agreement, DHL Express will purchase approximately 2 million U.S. gallons (around 6,000 metric tons) of SAF during the one-year term from July 2026 through June 2027. The volume is expected to cover approximately 50% of DHL Express’ fuel consumption at its Madrid gateway, representing a significant step forward in reducing emissions from air transport operations in Spain.

The SAF supplied under the agreement is produced from waste and residue feedstocks as defined in Annex IX parts A and B of the EU Renewable Energy Directive, including materials such as used cooking oil. Compared with conventional jet fuel, SAF can save around 80 % lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions reductions and plays a critical role in the decarbonization of aviation.

“Sustainable aviation fuel is one of the most effective levers currently available to reduce emissions from air freight transportation. This agreement with Moeve enables us to significantly increase the use of SAF at one of our key European gateways and demonstrates how collaboration across the aviation value chain can accelerate the transition to lower-emission logistics. By securing SAF volumes equivalent to around half of our fuel consumption in Madrid, we are making meaningful progress toward our goal of increasing SAF use to 30 percent by 2030,” emphasized Tomás Holgado, vice president Aviation, DHL Express Spain.

“This agreement with DHL Express marks another step forward in our strategy to accelerate the decarbonization of air transport through readily available and scalable solutions such as sustainable aviation fuels. Moeve has a firm commitment to becoming a leading European producer of second-generation biofuels, with production capacity already reaching 1.1 million tonnes per year. This capacity will grow significantly with the launch next year of our new SAF plant in Huelva, adding a further 500,000 tonnes. Partnerships such as this demonstrate that the energy transition moves faster when producers and customers work together to reduce emissions in sectors that are difficult to electrify, like aviation.”

text:
Rolls-Royce has announced its first 100% powered Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) flight, marking a key step in Gulfstream Aerospace’s high-altitude flight test campaign.

The journey involved Pearl 700 engines, powering a Gulfstream G800 flight.

This achievement demonstrates that SAF can be a reliable and sustainable option for aviation.

“The valuable insights we have gained from these latest tests at high altitudes, as well as the data from projects like QRITOS or ECLIF3, are driving real progress in understanding aviation’s non-CO₂ climate impacts and potential mitigation options.”

When isolating how different fuel compositions influence non-CO₂ emissions, it allows for a huge market in decarbonisation for aviation.

Creating neat SAF

Making SAF isn’t an easy job, it can involve high costs, feedstock shortages and complex processing methods.

To overcome these common steps, the team compared Jet-A aviation fuel, low-sulfur Jet-A and Hydro-processed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA), containing no sulfur or aromatics.

Results from the experiment show that there was a significant reduction in particulate emissions when using neat SAF, reducing the amount of contrail information.

The overarching results show that Rolls-Royce’s in-production Trent and business aviation engines have the capacity to operate with 100% SAF.

Rolls-Royce states that currently, “SAF is only certified for blends of up to 50% with conventional jet fuel.”

SAF has the potential to reduce CO₂ lifecycle emissions by up to 80% when compared to conventional jet fuel, calling for certification of a higher SAF-conventional jet fuel blend.

Rolls-Royce’s sustainability journey

Rolls-Royce views SAF as a key enabler of aviation decarbonisation, particularly for long-haul flights where gas turbine engines will remain essential for decades.

Alongside SAF adoption, the company continues to improve engine efficiency through technologies such as its UltraFan demonstrator, which is designed to deliver a 25% fuel burn improvement over the first Trent engine.

Rolls-Royce is also working with fuel producers, regulators, governments and industry partners to help scale the production, distribution and availability of qualified SAF.

These efforts support the company's commitment to achieving net zero across its operations by 2030 and enabling the aviation sector to reach net zero by 2050.

text:
The U.S. biofuel industry reached another milestone on July 28, 2026, as new federal data confirmed record soybean crush and renewable diesel production, highlighting how domestic energy policies are reshaping agricultural markets. The latest figures from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) show biofuel plants operating at or near full capacity following the implementation of larger Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs). The development matters because stronger soybean demand is providing fresh support for commodity prices while encouraging new investments across the U.S. agricultural supply chain.

The EPA's June Renewable Identification Number (RIN) report revealed that combined D4 and D5 RIN generation climbed to 862 million Renewable Volume Obligation gallons during June, representing a 33% increase from a year earlier. Even more significant for agriculture, renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel production reached a record 499 million gallons, reinforcing the industry's growing appetite for soybean oil. Analysts say this is not simply a seasonal surge but evidence of a long-term transformation driven by federal policy, renewable fuel incentives, and expanding domestic processing capacity that continues to reshape demand fundamentals for soybeans.

Federal policy becomes the engine behind record soybean crush

According to Susan Stroud, founder and CEO of NoBull Agriculture, the surge in soybean crush is primarily the consequence of the EPA's 2026 and 2027 Renewable Volume Obligations, finalized earlier this year. Those mandates require biodiesel and renewable diesel producers to maximize production in order to meet federal blending targets. More crushing facilities are expected to begin operations over the coming years, potentially pushing soybean processing to even higher records. For soybean growers, the policy shift represents a structural increase in domestic demand rather than a temporary market rally, creating a stronger foundation for long-term price support.

Biofuel demand is only one factor supporting soybean prices. China has resumed soybean purchases for the upcoming marketing year, while tighter global diesel supplies following Russian export restrictions have strengthened renewable fuel economics and lifted soybean oil values. At the same time, the 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit continues to improve profitability for both renewable diesel and ethanol producers. Industry analysts believe ethanol has quietly entered its own expansion phase, providing additional demand for corn alongside the headline growth occurring in soybean crush and renewable diesel production.
